blocks.heading: What this section asks you to do
blocks.text: Define a multinational company, explain why firms operate across borders, and weigh what they bring to a host country and to their home country.

blocks.heading: What a multinational company is
blocks.text: A multinational company (MNC) is a firm that produces goods or sells them in more than one country. The country of its head office is its home country; each country where it produces or sells is a host country. Most products a learner can name - drinks, phones, clothing - are made and sold this way, and the spread of these firms is one of the engines of globalisation: the same product, sold in many countries, often assembled in several of them.

blocks.heading: A plant opens in Oshakati
blocks.text: Haneda Electronics keeps its head office in Nagoya, Japan, and has opened an assembly plant in Oshakati. The plant pays 300 workers an average of N$6 500 a month, and the 60 technicians it trained now also maintain machinery for other firms in the town. Its profit, about N$12 million a year, is paid to the head office. The host country, Namibia, gains jobs, wages and skills that spread beyond the plant; the home country, Japan, gains profit and a market it did not serve before; and the cost that travels with them is that local electronics sellers now face a competitor with far larger resources behind it.

blocks.heading: Multinational is not a kind of ownership
blocks.text: Learners mix up three questions that sound alike. A public limited company sells its shares on a stock exchange - that is ownership traded to the public. A state-owned company belongs to a government - that is who owns it. A multinational company produces or sells in more than one country - that is where it operates. One firm may be any combination of the three: a state-owned airline that flies to and keeps offices in other countries is state-owned and multinational at once. The test: ask which question the sentence answers - ownership traded, who owns it, or where it operates.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The ownership forms named here are classified in topic 3.5; the trade these firms carry is priced by the exchange rates of topic 6.3; and whether their goods cross borders freely is the subject of the next section.
